actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
The title of the measure was amended. Agreed to without objection.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 421 - 1 (Roll no. 252).
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 421 - 1 (Roll no. 252).
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H4705-4706)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 1118.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H4656; text: CR H4656)
Mr. Burlison moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended.
Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
Committee Consideration and Mark-up Session Held

Referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, and in addition to the Committee on Armed Services, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

committees.name: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agencies procuring commercial supplies and services through the GSA multiple award schedule, and commercial vendors bidding on those contracts.
dimensions.evidence: contracts and orders under the multiple award schedule program of the General Services Administration (GSA) may be evaluated on best value

dimensions.assessment: Changes the evaluation criteria standard for certain federal procurement contracts from lowest cost to best value.
dimensions.evidence: striking 'lowest overall cost alternative' and inserting 'best value'.

dimensions.assessment: Potentially affects the pricing structure and spending outcomes of volume-buying commercial supplies and services across federal agencies, though specific monetary effects are unstated.
dimensions.evidence: The GSA's multiple award schedules provide federal agencies with a simplified process for obtaining commercial supplies and commercial services at prices associated with volume buying.

dimensions.assessment: Amends Section 152(3)(B) of title 41, United States Code, specifically addressing the GSA multiple award schedule program.
dimensions.evidence: Section 152(3)(B) of title 41, United States Code, is amended

dimensions.assessment: Provides a permanent statutory change to how GSA schedule contracts can be evaluated.
dimensions.evidence: Section 152(3)(B) of title 41, United States Code, is amended by striking 'lowest overall cost alternative' and inserting 'best value'.

missing_information: Quantitative estimates of cost differences resulting from best value versus lowest cost evaluations.
The volume or total monetary value of contracts affected.
importance_detail.rationale: Allows General Services Administration multiple award schedule contracts and orders to be evaluated on 'best value' instead of 'lowest overall cost alternative' when determined to be in the government's best interest.
